meta.disclaimer: These are rules of thumb used by macro traders to frame what the data is saying. They describe conditions, not predictions or trading advice. Edit any text or threshold below; the dashboard rebuilds from this file.
meta.how_bands_work: A band applies when the value is below its 'lt' number. Bands are checked top to bottom; the last band has no 'lt' and catches everything above.

10y-2y.title: 10Y - 2Y
10y-2y.what: Classic curve slope. Compares what the market expects policy rates to do over the next two years against the 10-year yield.

bands.label: Deeply inverted
bands.meaning: Short rates sit far above long rates. The market is pricing a policy rate that is too tight for the economy and eventual cuts.
bands.so_what: Historically a recession warning with a long and variable lag (often 6-24 months). Not a timing tool by itself.

bands.label: Inverted
bands.meaning: 2Y yield is above the 10Y. Markets expect policy rates to fall later.
bands.so_what: Late-cycle or restrictive-policy signal. Watch for the un-inversion (re-steepening): it has often come right before or during downturns.

bands.label: Flat
bands.meaning: Little compensation for holding longer maturities. Growth and rate expectations are roughly balanced.
bands.so_what: Transition zone. The direction of the next move (steepening or inverting) matters more than the level.

bands.label: Normal / positive
bands.meaning: Healthy upward slope. Investors want extra yield for duration, consistent with growth and some inflation risk.
bands.so_what: Neutral to supportive backdrop for risk assets. A fast move up from inversion is a different story: see the steepener type below.

bands.label: Steep
bands.meaning: Wide gap between long and short yields. Either policy is easy and growth is expected to pick up, or the long end is demanding a large term premium.
bands.so_what: Check the cause: falling 2Y (cuts priced) is a different signal than rising 10Y (inflation, supply, term premium).

10y-3m.title: 10Y - 3M
10y-3m.what: Compares the 10-year yield with the current policy rate (3-month bill). The NY Fed's recession-probability model uses this spread.

bands.label: Deeply inverted
bands.meaning: The policy rate is well above the 10Y yield. Policy is clearly restrictive relative to long-term expectations.
bands.so_what: Strongest traditional recession-risk reading. Timing remains uncertain; sustained inversion for months carries more weight than a brief dip.

bands.label: Inverted
bands.meaning: 3M bill yields more than the 10Y.
bands.so_what: Recession risk is elevated historically. Cross-check with the 10Y-2Y: when both are inverted the signal is more convincing.

bands.label: Flat to modest
bands.meaning: Policy rate is close to the 10Y yield. Not much cushion for the long end.
bands.so_what: Neutral. Watch the next policy meeting and how fast the 3M moves.

bands.label: Positive
bands.meaning: 10Y yield comfortably above the policy rate. No inversion warning.
bands.so_what: Curve is not flagging recession risk on this measure.

20y-10y.title: 20Y - 10Y
20y-10y.what: Slope of the long end of the curve. Shows how much extra yield investors demand to go from 10 to 20 years: a read on term premium, long-duration supply, and pension/insurer demand.

bands.label: Long-end inverted
bands.meaning: The 20Y yields less than the 10Y. Unusual. It can reflect strong long-duration demand (pensions, insurers), flight to safety into long bonds, or a technical distortion: the 20Y is a less liquid point and its auctions can push the yield around.
bands.so_what: Do not read this like the 10Y-2Y. A negative 20Y-10Y is more often a liquidity and technical story than a recession call. Confirm with the 30Y-5Y and the 10Y-2Y before drawing conclusions.

bands.label: Very flat
bands.meaning: Little extra yield for stretching from 10 to 20 years. Long-end term premium is compressed.
bands.so_what: Long bonds are priced rich relative to the 10Y. If inflation or supply worries return, this is the zone where the long end can reprice sharply.

bands.label: Normal
bands.meaning: Typical modest upward slope at the long end.
bands.so_what: No stress signal. Use the direction of change over 5-20 days instead of the level.

bands.label: Steep
bands.meaning: Investors are demanding a lot of extra yield for long duration: higher term premium, heavy long-bond supply, or inflation and fiscal worries.
bands.so_what: Often accompanies a long-end sell-off (bear steepening). Headwind for long-duration assets. Check whether the 10Y itself is also rising.

30y-5y.title: 30Y - 5Y
30y-5y.what: Wide view of the curve from the belly to the very long end. Less affected by the 2Y's sensitivity to the next Fed move.

bands.label: Inverted
bands.meaning: Long bonds yield less than the 5Y. Market expects falling rates or sees little inflation risk over the long run.
bands.so_what: Defensive or late-cycle signal. Supports the case made by the 10Y-2Y and 10Y-3M if they are also inverted.

bands.label: Flat
bands.meaning: Limited term premium across the curve.
bands.so_what: Neutral. Watch direction.

bands.label: Steep
bands.meaning: The long end offers a large pickup over the 5Y: term premium, inflation, or supply pressure.
bands.so_what: Long-end stress or a reflation backdrop. Compare with real yields to separate the two.

dynamics.note: Classifies how a spread moved over the last 20 trading days. Direction of the spread plus whether yields were generally falling (bull) or rising (bear).

stable.label: Little change
stable.meaning: The spread has barely moved over 20 days.
stable.so_what: No new curve information. Level bands above still apply.

bull_steepener.label: Bull steepener
bull_steepener.meaning: Spread is widening because short yields are falling faster than long yields.
bull_steepener.so_what: Market is pricing rate cuts, often as growth weakens. Historically common into and during easing cycles.

bear_steepener.label: Bear steepener
bear_steepener.meaning: Spread is widening because long yields are rising faster than short yields.
bear_steepener.so_what: Inflation, supply, or term-premium pressure at the long end. Usually negative for bonds and long-duration equities.

bull_flattener.label: Bull flattener
bull_flattener.meaning: Spread is narrowing because long yields are falling faster than short yields.
bull_flattener.so_what: Flight to safety or falling long-run growth and inflation expectations.

bear_flattener.label: Bear flattener
bear_flattener.meaning: Spread is narrowing because short yields are rising faster than long yields.
bear_flattener.so_what: Market is pricing a tighter policy path. Typical when the Fed is hiking or turning hawkish.

zscore.note: How stretched a reading is versus its own 1-year (252 trading days) or 52-week average.

real_yield.title: 10Y real yield (TIPS)
real_yield.what: Inflation-adjusted 10-year yield. The opportunity cost of holding assets that pay no yield, such as gold.

bands.label: Very low vs 1y
bands.meaning: Real yields are far below their one-year average.
bands.so_what: Typically supportive for gold and growth assets.

bands.label: Normal range
bands.meaning: Real yields are close to their one-year average.
bands.so_what: No strong signal from level. Use the 5-20 day change.

bands.label: High vs 1y
bands.meaning: Real yields are well above their one-year average.
bands.so_what: Headwind for gold and long-duration assets. Cash and bonds pay a high real return.

dxy.title: US Dollar Index (DXY)
dxy.what: Dollar against a basket dominated by EUR, JPY and GBP. A stronger dollar tightens global financial conditions and usually weighs on gold and commodities.

bands.label: Very weak vs 1y
bands.meaning: The dollar is far below its one-year average.
bands.so_what: Supportive for gold and commodities. Watch for oversold bounces.

bands.label: Weak vs 1y
bands.meaning: The dollar is below its one-year average.
bands.so_what: Mild tailwind for gold and non-USD assets.

bands.label: Normal range
bands.meaning: The dollar is near its one-year average.
bands.so_what: No strong signal from level.

bands.label: Strong vs 1y
bands.meaning: The dollar is above its one-year average.
bands.so_what: Mild headwind for gold and commodities.

bands.label: Very strong vs 1y
bands.meaning: The dollar is far above its one-year average.
bands.so_what: Strong headwind for gold. Also a stretched move: watch for reversals when positioning is crowded.

usd_index.title: USD Index positioning (CFTC COT)
usd_index.what: ICE US Dollar Index futures, Legacy report, Non-Commercial (large speculators). Net = longs minus shorts. The COT Index scales today's net position between its 52-week low (0) and high (100).

bands.label: Extreme short
bands.meaning: Speculators are about as bearish on the dollar as they have been in a year.
bands.so_what: Crowded shorts. Fuel for a short-covering rally if the dollar stops falling. Contrarian bullish-dollar signal, needs a catalyst.

bands.label: Net short side
bands.meaning: Speculators are leaning bearish on the dollar relative to the past year.
bands.so_what: Trend is bearish dollar. Not yet crowded.

bands.label: Middle of range
bands.meaning: Positioning is neither stretched long nor short.
bands.so_what: No positioning edge. Use price action and yields.

bands.label: Net long side
bands.meaning: Speculators are leaning bullish on the dollar relative to the past year.
bands.so_what: Trend is bullish dollar. Room remains before it gets crowded.

bands.label: Extreme long
bands.meaning: Speculators are about as bullish on the dollar as they have been in a year.
bands.so_what: Crowded longs. Dollar is vulnerable to a sharp reversal if data or the Fed disappoints. Contrarian bearish-dollar signal, needs a catalyst.

gold.title: Gold positioning (CFTC COT)
gold.what: COMEX Gold futures, Legacy Futures Only report, Non-Commercial traders (large speculators). This is the same report type as the USD Index figures, so the two can be compared with each other.

bands.label: Extreme short
bands.meaning: Managed money is about as bearish on gold as it has been in a year.
bands.so_what: Washed-out positioning. Downside fuel is mostly spent; a bounce needs a catalyst.

bands.label: Net short side
bands.meaning: Managed money is leaning away from gold relative to the past year.
bands.so_what: Weak conviction. Watch whether real yields and the dollar start to ease.

bands.label: Middle of range
bands.meaning: Positioning is neither stretched long nor short.
bands.so_what: No positioning edge.

bands.label: Net long side
bands.meaning: Managed money is leaning long gold relative to the past year.
bands.so_what: Trend is supported by speculators. Vulnerable if real yields or the dollar rise.

bands.label: Extreme long
bands.meaning: Managed money is about as bullish on gold as it has been in a year.
bands.so_what: Crowded longs. A hawkish surprise can trigger fast liquidation.

cross_signals.label: Gold headwind: real yields and dollar both rising
cross_signals.meaning: 10Y real yield is up over 20 days and the dollar index is up more than 1%. Both raise the opportunity cost of holding gold.

cross_signals.label: Gold tailwind: real yields and dollar both falling
cross_signals.meaning: 10Y real yield is down over 20 days and the dollar index is down more than 1%. Both lower the opportunity cost of holding gold.

cross_signals.label: Dollar rally with crowded long positioning
cross_signals.meaning: DXY is well above its 1-year average and speculators are near their 52-week max long. The move is extended and positioning is vulnerable.

cross_signals.label: Dollar weakness with crowded short positioning
cross_signals.meaning: DXY is well below its 1-year average and speculators are near their 52-week max short. Short-covering risk is high.

cross_signals.label: Both 10Y-2Y and 10Y-3M are inverted
cross_signals.meaning: Two independent curve measures agree. The recession-risk signal is stronger than when only one is inverted. Timing remains uncertain.

cross_signals.label: Long-end sell-off
cross_signals.meaning: The 10Y yield is rising fast and the 20Y-10Y spread is widening. Pressure is concentrated in long duration: term premium, supply, or inflation worries.

cross_signals.label: Gold crowded long while real yields rise
cross_signals.meaning: Managed money is near its 52-week max long in gold while 10Y real yields are rising. This mix has historically been vulnerable to liquidation.

spread_default.what: Long yield minus short yield, in percentage points. Positive means the curve slopes upward between the two maturities; negative means it is inverted.

bands.label: Inverted
bands.meaning: The longer maturity yields less than the shorter one. The market is pricing lower rates ahead or demanding little term premium.
bands.so_what: Treat as a caution flag for growth, and check the 10Y-2Y and 10Y-3M for confirmation.

bands.label: Flat
bands.meaning: Very little extra yield for holding the longer maturity.
bands.so_what: Transition zone. The direction of the next move matters more than the level.

bands.label: Positive slope
bands.meaning: A normal upward slope between these two maturities.
bands.so_what: No stress signal from this pair on its own. Watch the 5-20 day direction.

bands.label: Steep
bands.meaning: A wide gap between the two maturities: front-end rate cuts priced in, or higher term premium at the long end.
bands.so_what: Check whether it is a bull steepener (yields falling, front end leading) or a bear steepener (yields rising, long end leading).
